# Hardware encoder<AvailableFrom v="4.0.544" />

Which hardware encoder family to use on Windows and Linux when [hardware acceleration](/docs/options/hardware-acceleration) is enabled. One of "nvenc" (NVIDIA) or "qsv" (Intel Quick Sync Video). Only applies to H.264 and H.265. On macOS, VideoToolbox is always used.<br />If not set, Remotion tries NVENC first, then QSV, and uses the first one that can encode a test frame on this machine. If none works, "if-possible" falls back to software encoding and "required" throws an error that says why each encoder failed.<br />With "qsv" and no `crf` or `videoBitrate` set, Remotion uses intelligent constant quality (ICQ) with look-ahead, because QSV has no usable default quality target. The default ICQ value is 23, which scored VMAF 97 to 98 on the content we tested; set the `REMOTION_QSV_QUALITY` environment variable to change it (higher is smaller and lower quality).<br />Your FFmpeg build must include the QSV encoders (Remotion's bundled FFmpeg does not) and the audio encoder Remotion uses (`libfdk_aac`), and you pass it with `binariesDirectory`. The `REMOTION_HW_ENCODER` environment variable is also read when neither the CLI flag nor the config option is set.

## CLI flag

```text
--hardware-encoder <value>
```

The following CLI commands accept this option:

- [`remotion studio`](/docs/cli/studio)
- [`remotion render`](/docs/cli/render)
- [`remotion benchmark`](/docs/cli/benchmark)

## APIs that have this option

The following APIs accept this option:

- [`renderMedia()`](/docs/renderer/render-media#hardwareencoder)
- [`stitchFramesToVideo()`](/docs/renderer/stitch-frames-to-video#hardwareencoder)

## Config file

```ts twoslash title="remotion.config.ts"
import {Config} from '@remotion/cli/config';
// ---cut---
Config.setHardwareAcceleration('if-possible');
Config.setHardwareEncoder('qsv');
```
